This petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1994 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 09.092023 at about 6.45 p.m. Mahendra Kumar was walking infront of Byrava Condiments, JMJ Hospital Road, Nagavara, Bengaluru, at that time, a concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AJ-7764 being driven by its driver at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against Mahendra Kumar from behind, due to this impact, he fell down and left back side wheel of the lorry ran over his body, as a result SCCH 5 said Mahendra Kumar succumbed to the fatal injuries on the spot.

Thereafter post mortem was conducted at Dr.B.R.Ambedkar Hospital and body was handed over to the petitioners, who performed funeral and obsequies by spending Rs.2,00,000/- and they have also spent a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- for transportation and other consequential expenses.

Prior to the accident, deceased Mahendra Kumar was hale and healthy, aged about 50 years,
working in two shifts i.e., at morning he was working as housekeeping at Chris American Hospital,
Nagavara and as a watchman (security guard) at West Inn Co-Stay, Paying Guest at Nagavara,
thereby earning Rs.35,000/- p.m.
Petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are daughters of the deceased/Mahendra Kumar, they were entirely depending on income of the deceased.
Due to untimely death of deceased, petitioners are suffering from SCCH 5 mental shock and financial problems.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AJ-7764 by its driver and K.G.Halli police have registered a case in crime No.59/2023.
The respondent No.1 being the owner of the said lorry and respondent No.2 being the insurer, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- to the petitioners with interest.

4. In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1/ owner has appeared through his counsel,
but not chosen to file written statement.
Respondent No.2/insurer has filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

Further submitted that, a Concrete Mixer Lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-AJ-7764 was not at all involved in the alleged accident.
Further submitted issuance of Miscellaneous Vehicle Package Policy in respect of alleged lorry and it was valid as on SCCH 5 the date of accident.

Further submitted that, scope of the policy is only as per the terms and conditions of policy issued to the Concrete Mixer Lorry and it covers the risk or damage in the construction plant only, not on public road and it is not a motor policy.
Further submitted that, driver of the offending vehicle did not possessed valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further denied dependency of the petitioners on deceased, age, occupation and income of the deceased.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further respondent No.2 is entitled to take defence available under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, the court has framed the following:
SCCH 5 ::ISSUES::
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Mahendra Kumar, S/o. Late.
Shanmugam died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 09.09.2023 at about 6.45 p.m.
infront of Byrava Condiments, JMJ Hospital Road, Nagavara, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving of Concrete Mixer Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AJ-7764 dashed against the deceased and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 /wife of the deceased has deposed her evidence as PW-1 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
Per contra, respondents have not adduced any evidence.

sentences.text: Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8.
Issue No.1:- The petitioners inorder to prove their case, petitioner No.1/wife of the deceased is examined as PW-1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated petition averments.

Though she has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the evidence of the PW-1.
9.

Apart from the oral evidence, the PW-1 has got marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as SCCH 5 Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of inquest is marked as Ex.P.6 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.8, which corroborates the case of the petitioners about causing of the accident dated 09.09.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement by respondent No.2, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners about causing of death of Mahendra Kumar out of the accident held on 09.09.2023 at about 6.45 p.m. when he was walking infront of Byrava Condiments, JMJ Hospital Road, Nagavara, Bengaluru.

In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments SCCH 5 advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
11.
The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of Concrete Mixer Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AJ-7764.
Under such circumstances, believing the evidence of the petitioners, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-

As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/Mahendra Kumar was aged about 50 years as on the date of accident, for proof of age of the deceased, petitioners have not produced any age proof documents, but on perusal of copy of inquest marked as Ex.P.6, age of the deceased is mentioned as 50 years.

Accordingly relying on Ex.P.6, age of the deceased is considered SCCH 5 about 50 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 13 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was working as Housekeeper at Chris American Hospital, Nagavara, Bengaluru and during night hours he was working as Watchman (Security Guard) at West Inn Co- stay, Paying Guest at Nagavara, Bengaluru, thereby earning Rs.35,000/-
p.m.

To prove the said fact, petitioners have exhibited hospital endorsements issued by Chris Scan Hospital and West Inn Co-stay marked as Ex.P.7, wherein it is clearly mentioned that, deceased Mahendra Kumar was drawing salary of Rs.15,000/- p.m. and Rs.20,000/- p.m. respectively.
Further in this regard, petitioners have not examined the authors of Ex.P.7.

Under such circumstances, with SCCH 5 reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.15,250/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency.

sentences.text: 14. Further petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are daughters of the deceased Mahendra Kumar.

To prove the said facts, they have furnished study certificate issued by Reva Independent PU College, Kattigenahalli, Bengaluru marked as Ex.P.9 and copies of aadhar cards of the petitioner No.1 to 3 is on record., which reveals that, they are legal representatives of the deceased Mahendra Kumar.

15. As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 2 to 3, then 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the SCCH 5 deceased, so that, 1/3rd of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

16. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 25% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged in between 40 to 50 years, in case of self employed person or person having fixed salary as future prospects.

 (i) Monthly Income Rs.15,250/-

Monthly income Rs.12,708/-
(iv) Compensation after Rs.12,708/- x Rs.19,82,448/-
multiplier of 13 is 12 x 13 applied 18.
Further petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased is entitled for Rs.20,000/- towards consortium.

Petitioner No.2 and 3 being the daughters of the deceased is entitled for Rs.20,000/-
towards loss of parental consortium.
Further they are entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/- and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/-.

19. The details of compensation awarded is as under:
SCCH 5 Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 19,82,448-00 2. Loss of consortium 20,000-00 (Petitioner No.1)
3. Loss of parental consortium 40,000-00 (Rs.20,000/- each to Petitioner No.2 & 3)
4. Loss of Estate 15,000-00 5.
Funeral Expenses 15,000-00 Total 20,72,448-00 20.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.20,72,448/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

21. Ofcourse during the course of arguments, respondent No.2 counsel argued that, this is pedestrian negligence case and deceased has crossed the road without observing the vehicles, his contributory negligence also involved to the case on hand for an extent SCCH 5 of 10 to 15% and as per the sketch, accident was occurred in the middle of the road etc., but to substantiate the said arguments, there is no sufficient evidence on respondent side, hence said arguments are not supports the respondents case.

22. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.3008/286906201/0007746 in respect of lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AJ-7746 which is valid for the period from 07.04.2023 to 06.04.2024, the alleged accident was occurred on 09.09.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With SCCH 5 these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.20,72,448/- (Rupees Twenty Lakhs Seventy Two Thousand Four Hundred Forty Eight Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 60:20:20 in the award amount.
SCCH 5 The petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.

Since Petitioner No.3 is minor, on deposit of the award amount, entire share shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank till she attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor petitioner guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor petitioner.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
